criteria_results.evidence: PlayerMana.cs diff adds `public void ResetMana() { CurrentMana = maxMana; timeSinceLastSpend = postCastRegenDelay; }`, mirroring Awake()'s already-elapsed timer convention. This restores current mana to full and returns the regen-delay timer to a non-blocking state, matching GDD §5 line 300-301's owner-controlled reset/spend interface for restart orchestration.

PlayerMana.cs adds `public event Action<float> CastDenied;`, invoked only in the `amount > CurrentMana` branch of Spend (insufficient-mana refusal), never on success (ManaSpent fires instead) and never on the amount<=0 no-op path. This is a distinct signal from a successful spend, matching GDD §3 'Failure is readable' / low mana.

PlayerMana.cs's only new members are ResetMana and CastDenied; no spell-local cooldown/charge/cast/placement/active-field members were added. The new PlayerMana_PublicApiSurface_OnlyOwnsManaAndRegenDelayState test locks the declared public surface to {CastDenied, CurrentMana, ManaSpent, MaxMana, PostCastRegenDelay, ResetMana, Spend, Tick}, matching GDD §2/§5 ownership boundary text.

PlayerManaPlayModeTests.cs was extended with new UnityTest/Test cases covering ResetMana, CastDenied, and PlayerManaUI flash/revert behavior, satisfying the 'extended' half of this gate at the source level. However, neither role executed the suite (test author explicitly states 'No tests were executed'), so whether existing and new Play Mode coverage 'continues to pass' is unproven per the no-execution-claims policy.

New tests assert color-flash logic via reflection-driven in-memory GameObjects, but this gate requires validating that failure is actually readable, which is runtime/perceptual and was not executed or human-verified; the test author's own known_limitations explicitly call out that human Play Mode/visual verification of the real scene's mana indicator flashing is still required.

Readability of low-mana failure through the mana indicator to an actual player is a human/runtime judgment per UNITY_TESTING_POLICY.md ('Human runtime validation... readability... wherever source-level assertions cannot prove quality'). No Unity execution or human visual check was performed by either role, so this gate is not proven despite the color-flash implementation and tests being logically sound at the source level.

risks: No Play Mode test execution evidence exists for this change; VAL-001's 'continues to pass' claim and the new ResetMana/CastDenied/UI-flash tests are unverified at runtime.
Human visual verification of the actual blue mana-fill indicator flashing/reverting correctly in the committed DoorPrototype.unity scene has not occurred, per the test author's own stated limitation.

The very short possible deniedFlashDuration/frame-timing interaction (color reverts to normal within the same Update call once the countdown reaches zero) could occasionally suppress denied-flash visibility for a single low-framerate frame; not a correctness defect but worth a human framerate/readability check during Play Mode.
structured_output.summary: Candidate patch adds PlayerMana.ResetMana() (restores CurrentMana to maxMana and resets the post-cast regen-delay timer to an already-elapsed state) and a CastDenied event fired only on insufficient-mana refusal, distinct from ManaSpent, satisfying AC-001/AC-002 with no growth of PlayerMana's public surface beyond mana/regen-delay ownership (AC-003, locked by a reflection-based surface test). PlayerManaUI consumes CastDenied to flash the existing fill Image and correctly captures its normalColor from the actual fillImage.color in OnEnable rather than a hardcoded white default — confirmed necessary and correct against the committed scene, where the production fill Image's m_Color is blue (0,0,1,1), not white. Test coverage was extended for both new members and the color-capture regression, but no test execution or human Play Mode/visual verification was performed by either role, so the runtime completion gates remain unproven.
